idiom_name: trait + unit-struct no-op implementation (std::io::sink) / Option with unwrap_or
implementation_notes: Rust has no null, so the two realizations are explicit: a trait with a unit-struct implementation whose methods are empty - the standard library ships std::io::sink(), 'a writer which will move data into the void' that implements Write and Default, plus io::empty() for readers - and Option<T> with unwrap_or/map_or or a defaulted trait method when absence is a value the caller may act on. A trait can carry the neutral behaviour as a default method, which makes 'do nothing' the fallback for every implementor. Choose the null object when callers should stay uniform, Option when they must distinguish absent from present.
pitfalls: Option<Box<dyn Trait>> is not a null object: every call site still unwraps and the box adds a vtable; a generic parameter or a &dyn Trait default keeps the call unconditional.
A no-op Write implementation silently discards data the caller may assume was persisted - io::sink() belongs on pipelines that intentionally discard, not on a file that must exist.
Rust forces the null type to implement every trait method, but an unimplemented!()/todo!() body turns the neutral collaborator into a runtime panic; use a silently empty body deliberately.
